silicon-valley-girl.bio: Silicon Valley Girl interviews AI and tech leaders and translates what they ship into workflows for knowledge workers, creators, and non-engineers. She covers agents, vibe coding, and day-to-day AI productivity, and runs a free newsletter on tools and career strategy. Worth following if you want practitioner demos with the people building the stack, not just commentary.

videos.title: Head of ChatGPT & Codex: agents for normal people are HERE
videos.keyTakeaway: OpenAI’s head of ChatGPT and Codex says agents are finally reliable enough that non-technical knowledge workers will get the same leverage early adopters spent two years earning—within months, not years.
videos.executiveSummary: Silicon Valley Girl interviews Tibo, who runs ChatGPT, Codex, and the APIs at OpenAI, on why agents are crossing from technical early adopters into ordinary knowledge work. The conversation is a live working session as much as a talk: they run Codex against email, calendar, computer use, and a half-built content app while Tibo explains what matured (long-horizon reliability, browser/computer use, 100+ plugins, auto-review safety) and what still needs packaging. It responds to the gap between software engineering’s AI transformation—Google’s 75% AI-written code is the reference point—and everyone else’s still-manual research, inbox, and ops load. Tibo’s through-line is augmentation with humans still on the hook, plus a near-term shift of agent memory and files into the cloud so the same assistant follows you across devices.
videos.summary: Silicon Valley Girl interviews OpenAI’s Tibo (ChatGPT, Codex, APIs) on agents becoming reliable for non-technical knowledge workers within months. They demo live Codex workflows—scheduled research, inbox/calendar agents, computer use, skill creator—while he argues humans stay responsible and prompting skill stops being the main moat.
